summary: ```# Quick Start Part Two: How to Make a Maid Outfit? (p01 1_Making the Top) ## Introduction Hello everyone, I am Xueli. In this tutorial video, we will learn how to make this set of women's clothing. If you are a complete beginner user, you can watch our beginner entry video first. ## Importing the Model First, let's import a model into the library window. Double-click to import a T-shirt file into the library window. We can't directly copy the T-shirt file into the library window because it is not ready yet. So we need to arrange the template first. ## Template Adjustment Here we can see that this template is a bit too big for our model, Hannah. As a reference, let's first change the shape in the second window. Change the shape to full transparent. This way, we can refer to Hannah's body image to fully export the template. When we export, there is a basis we can refer to, specifically the shoulder line. First, we put the template on the line of the front middle and the virtual model. Then we place the shoulder here, referring to the line on the side of the waist, extending along the chest to the position near the shoulder point. After we export, we will align the templates little by little to see if they can be aligned. Now it's still a bit big, so we'll export it again and align the template. ## Finalizing the Template Now we can see if the shoulder points from the waist to the chest are indeed near; then we're almost done. We'll adjust the template slowly after we use this as the basis. Next, we will arrange the template around the virtual model. To do this, we need to press Shift + F to open the arrangement point. Click on the board and then click on the blue point. The board will be arranged around the virtual model. Because our board itself is symmetrical, when we arrange it on the arrangement point, the other side will also be automatically arranged. Finally, the back piece is arranged near the waist, like our board. After they are arranged, we can press Shift + F to hide the arrangement point. ## Checking Alignment You just need to refer to the position in my video. Press the number 2 key to go back to the front view. When rotating the view, we can see that the position of the front and back pieces is relatively low. When they are together, they may pass through the body of the virtual model. We try to avoid this kind of problem, so we have to move them. In the process of adjusting the arrangement of the board, try not to cross-check with the model. Press Ctrl + Z to return. Then press the control key to turn on the model. Because the default T-shirt in the software has the effect of the sewing line itself, and we arranged it well before around the virtual model, the T-shirt is directly worn on the virtual model, Hannah. ## Adjusting the Board Now we will start adjusting the board. First of all, we can find the line 3D board tool in the 3D window. Click on the clothing to draw some straight lines. Double-click to complete the creation of this line. Then we turn to the back and continue clicking to draw the line. In the process of clicking, press the control key to create a curve point. Press ESC to cancel the creation and start drawing again. After drawing, double-click to complete. Remember to connect to the outside line of the board. We then use the edit dot tool to choose all the lines. Press the Shift key to select more. After choosing, in the menu bar in the right-hand corner, choose the option below the symmetrical column. This board will be based on the 3D line we just drew on the clothing to cut. ## Final Adjustments Next, we can select the extra boards and delete them by pressing the Delete key. Then we press the control key to simulate. Now we can see that there is still some distance between the clothing and the virtual model. After selecting the virtual model in the attribute editor, you can adjust its surface diameter to 1. After opening the simulation, you will see that the clothing is closer to the virtual model. This is because the air thickness around the virtual model is reduced to 1 mm. When the view is a little farther away, we will find that its shoulders are not in harmony; it looks like there is more. So we use the edit board tool to find the point where the shoulders lean in, then move this point. Press the control key to drag along its original rhythm. We drag it inward a little to quickly match the board position. ## Simulation and Elasticity You can click in the 3D window, where there will be a blue dot. Then we can find the point to move. After dragging and opening the simulation, you will see that the shoulder line is closer now. Next, let's learn how to achieve the draw effect. First of all, we press the Shift key and select all these lines that form the collar. Then go to the attribute editor and find the elastic option to hook it up. After opening the simulation, the collar will tighten. If this elastic ratio is smaller, it will tighten more. However, because our current particle diameter is set to the default of 20, we can't see the wrinkles. So we have to reduce the particle diameter to 10 to display the wrinkles on the collar. The smaller the particle diameter, the more the grid, and the more details we can see. ## Conclusion Finally, we can reduce the conflict thickness. If we reduce the conflict thickness, the air thickness around the board will also be reduced. This way, the costume will look more intimate. Let's take a look at the front chest; there seems to be a small amount of wrinkles. To address this, we have to make it wider in the front and middle, increasing the fabric in front of the chest. Using the edit tool, select the whole front and middle line, pull it out, and increase this piece of fabric. If our fabric is increased, we have to reduce the elastic ratio a little bit to make it tighter. This is important because the top and outside will be a tight women's dress. We need to use the shrink rate to shrink the whole board into a tight state. The shrink rate is divided into the front and the back. Using the edit tool, after selecting the middle board, we will see an arrow. The arrow direction indicates our front, and it is at a 90-degree angle at the end. Now we have to make it tight horizontally by reducing the end shrink rate a little bit. Here we can gradually reduce the end shrink rate from 100 to 70, so the dress becomes a tight dress. Finally, we can freeze the board. ```
